data.name: Azali
data.gender_notes: Azali is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word 'azala' which means 'he supported' or 'he aided'. Azali is a name of strength and support, often given to children born into families with strong values and a sense of duty towards their community. The name Azali carries the meaning “Strong support” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Azali usually hope their child will grow to embody strong support and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name of strength and support in times of need
data.etymology: Azali belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong support.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Azali total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Al-'Ibar', Chapter 6: The Berbers and the Foundation of the Kingdom of the Banu Marin in the Maghreb
historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun describes the Berber tribes Azali and Beni Chleuh, who lived in the region of the present-day Middle Atlas. He mentions that both tribes were composed of free men and had a strong military organization. He notes that the Azali were more warlike and powerful than the Beni Chleuh.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Maqqari's 'Nafh Al-Tib', Volume II: The Foundation of the Almohad Dynasty The name Azali carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Maqqari recounts the story of the Berber leader Buluggin ibn Ziri, who is said to have founded the city of Al-Qasr al-Kabir (present-day Sebha) and established the Azali state in the central Maghreb. He also mentions that the Azali were a powerful Berber confederation who controlled a significant part of the Maghreb in the 11th century.
